title: Why Are Multiple Drains Clogged at the Same Time?

seo.meta_description: When several drains slow down or back up at the same time, the restriction is often downstream of where their pipes join rather than in each individual trap.

content_html:
When several drains slow down or back up at the same time, the restriction is often downstream of where their pipes join rather than in each individual trap. A toilet bubbling when the washer drains, or water rising in a low shower, points toward a main-line restriction. Avoid sending large volumes of water down the system while you determine the scope.

Map which fixtures are affected and on which level

If only one sink is slow, start locally. If a toilet, shower, and sink in the same area react to one another, the problem is likely in a common branch. Multiple levels or the lowest fixture backing up can point toward the main line.

Stop using water if sewage begins backing up

Do not keep testing showers, the washer, or dishwasher to see whether it improves. Every discharge adds volume behind the blockage. Keep people and pets away from sewage and use appropriate protection during later cleanup.

Do not mix chemical drain openers in a shared line

Products poured into different drains can meet in the same piping and create a hazardous exposure for anyone opening the system. Tell a plumber about any chemical already used before work begins.

A main-line blockage usually needs appropriate equipment

Roots, buildup, damaged pipe, or a lodged object may require professional cabling, camera inspection, or repair. If backups repeat, multiple drains are affected, or cleanouts overflow, stop using the system and arrange service.
